transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-13
Start time: 16:00 EST
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Redwood CSM); James Holloway (Oakridge - Procurement), Aisha Khan (Oakridge - Legal), Ravi Patel (Oakridge - CTO), Sophie Liu (Oakridge - Security)

Summary:
Brief legal/procurement review of Redwood MSA and DPA, discuss SLA stack and pricing approval path, confirm security artifacts and vendor onboarding timeline. Customer has an internal procurement milestone in early Dec; they want a pilot and vendor onboarding checklist.

Topics: MSA redlines, DPA data residency & retention, SLA uptime and credits, encryption/KMS, SSO/SAML, audit logs, pricing approval, pilot/onboarding timeline.

[00:00:08] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for taking the time, appreciate it. Uh, we'll run through the redlines and questions you sent, go through SLA and security items, and then lay out next steps.
[00:00:22] James Holloway: Thanks Maya, yes we want to get clarity on the DPA retention and the SLA credits, and also sequential approval path for pricing - finance needs a number by next week ideally.
[00:00:35] Diego Ramos: Hi all, Diego here, I'll focus on the technical/security items and the private deployment options, VPC peering, HSM/KMS integration.
[00:00:48] Aisha Khan: Hi, Aisha from legal. We redlined the MSA, large chunk around liability cap and indemnity, also a few questions in the DPA about subprocessors and breach notification timelines.

[00:02:10] Maya Chen: Great, starting with the MSA - on the liability cap we proposed standard carveouts; we can walk our legal team's language. I know you asked for a higher cap tied to fees, is that right James?
[00:02:28] James Holloway: Right, procurement would prefer 12 months of fees, legal would like to see some exceptions for gross negligence. We're open to a tiered approach with higher caps for enterprise customers, we just need explicit language to pass it through my finance org.
[00:02:45] Aisha Khan: Also requesting clearer SLA credit calculation, the existing formula in section 5 reads opaque. We want a clear credit schedule and max cumulative credits per year.
[00:03:00] Maya Chen: Understood. On SLA, Redwood's standard is 99.9% for hosted API and enterprise SLAs for Dedicated/private can be 99.95 with contractual credits. We'll attach our SLA spreadsheet, I can mark the specific rows to match your ask.

[00:04:20] Diego Ramos: For private deployment, the performance SLAs differ a bit because latency SLOs depend on colocated infra. But we do support Dedicated pools with SLA-backed throughput and region pinning, and can commit to an uptime SLA in the MSA for those clusters.
[00:04:38] Ravi Patel: One question - on the DPA, will Redwood allow for an audit right or do you only provide SOC2 and summary reports? Our security team sometimes requires audit rights for critical vendors.
[00:04:52] Priya Patel: Hi, Priya - we generally provide SOC 2 Type II, pen test summaries, and can enable time-limited attestations or third-party assessments under scoped conditions. Direct audit rights are unusual but we can discuss a negotiated clause for enterprise.

[00:06:05] Sophie Liu: For KMS, we need to know if Redwood supports customer-managed keys (BYOK) or HSM integration, especially for private deployments. Also, what about key rotation policies?
[00:06:18] Diego Ramos: Yes, we support customer KMS integration for Private and Dedicated; for hosted we offer envelope encryption with customer-managed keys via supported cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS). HSM-backed keys are possible for on-prem package. Rotation policies are configurable and we can documentation with diagrams.

[00:08:00] Aisha Khan: Regarding subprocessors listed in the DPA - we flagged Broadly named infra providers; can you provide a subprocessor list and adoption notice period when they change?
[00:08:16] Maya Chen: We'll provide current subprocessor list and agree to an advance notice window (standard is 30 days) for new subprocessors, and we'll manage redlines about notification and objection windows.

[00:09:50] James Holloway: Pricing - our procurement team needs a committed monthly cost for Dedicated vs hosted projection. We also need to understand burst/overage pricing and whether SSO/SSO integrations are included or an add-on.
[00:10:05] Maya Chen: I'll share the pricing approval sheet; core SSO/SAML enterprise SSO is included for Redwood Private and Dedicated enterprise tiers, hosted may be an add-on depending on plan. For burst, we can do reserved baseline with burst charges; I'll call out the numbers in the sheet.

[00:11:40] Ravi Patel: Technical pilot - we want to run a 2-week pilot internal PoC to validate latency and KPS for our use-case (real-time credit decisioning). Can Redwood support a sample load test and provide KV cache behavior and batching settings recommendations?
[00:11:58] Diego Ramos: Absolutely. We'll run a short benchmark with your prompt sets. We'll propose recommended runtime config: batching size, quantization profile, and KV cache settings. We can also provide a test harness and a pass/fail criteria doc.

[00:13:22] Sophie Liu: Data residency - even with encryption we need to ensure PII never leaves region X. In private deployment that is fine but for hosted we need a firm commitment on region pinning and logs residency.
[00:13:36] Priya Patel: We support region pinning in Dedicated and Private. For hosted, we have region options and can restrict processing to certain cloud regions; we will confirm logs and audit retention locations in the security packet.

[00:15:00] Aisha Khan: Breach notification timeline - we requested 48 hours in the DPA, current Redwood DPA says 72. Is 48 negotiable? That difference is a blocker for our legal.
[00:15:15] Maya Chen: I'll flag that with our legal; historically we do 72 hours, but for enterprise agreements we can often negotiate 48 hours with appropriate clauses. We'll bring a proposed redline.

[00:16:40] James Holloway: Also, procurement needs to know the PO issuance and payment terms. Our default is net-45 with PO required. Do you accept PO and net-45?
[00:16:52] Maya Chen: Redwood accepts PO; net-45 is fine for enterprise deals, though initial onboarding invoices sometimes default to net-30 until billing setup completeswe can note that in the pricing sheet for your finance team.

[00:18:30] Diego Ramos: A quick technical note on audit logs - we collect request/response logs for troubleshooting and can export logs to your SIEM or provide S3-compatible archives with retention controls. We can also mask or omit model outputs from logs on request to reduce PII retention.
[00:18:53] Sophie Liu: Good, we will want log export to our Splunk instance and an SLA on log delivery cadence.

[00:20:10] Maya Chen: I'll add a line item for log export cadence and format to the security packet.

[00:21:45] Aisha Khan: One more legal item - indemnity around model outputs, hallucination risk. We redlined limited liability for generated outputs that cause downstream issues. How has Redwood handled this with other financial customers?
[00:22:02] Priya Patel: Industry norm is to disclaim downstream liability for model outputs, but we can include mutual representations and a clause about permitted use and monitoring. For financial customers we add explicit mitigations and monitoring obligations.

[00:24:00] James Holloway: Timeline: Our committee meets on 2026-11-29 to sign final vendor contracts. We need a finalizeable MSA and pricing sheet by 2026-11-24 to route through legal and finance. Is that feasible?
[00:24:13] Maya Chen: Yes, it's tight but feasible. Maya: we'll target 11/17 for redline delivery, security packet by 11/18, then final MSA edits by 11/24. You'll have the pricing sheet with clear line items by 11/17 as well.

[00:25:40] Ravi Patel: For pilot environment, will we have a dedicated model variant and ability to pin model versions? We need deterministic behavior across runs.
[00:25:53] Diego Ramos: You can pin model versions and we support model variants; for the pilot we'll suggest a stable open model quant profile and lock the runtime config so you get reproducible behavior.

[00:27:30] Sophie Liu: Any additional compliance packages we need to buy for audit logs retention beyond standard?
[00:27:44] Maya Chen: We have add-ons: extended audit retention, SSO provisioning, and fedramp-like controls for on-prem/private setups. We'll list costs in the pricing sheet.

[00:29:10] James Holloway: On the DPA change control - if Redwood adds a new subprocessor and we object, what's the process? We need a formal 30 day review window and ability to terminate in limited circ.
[00:29:24] Aisha Khan: Yes, and we want a right to object clause with steps.
[00:29:30] Maya Chen: We can include a 30-day notice and a COOP (course of performance) clause to work through objections; termination for material breach tied to subprocessor changes is something our legal needs to evaluate, we'll propose text.

[00:31:10] Priya Patel: Quick note on onboarding: we provide a vendor onboarding checklist that covers SSO, key exchange, IP allowlists, contact points, and runbooks for the pilot. We'll share the checklist after this call.

[00:32:02] Diego Ramos: For the pilot benchmark, please share the prompt set and target qps/latency. We'll instrument telemetry and send an initial report within 72 hours of the test.

[00:33:20] James Holloway: I also want clarity on termination assistance - how long will Redwood keep customer data after termination and what's the export format?
[00:33:34] Maya Chen: Standard is 30 days data retention on termination for export, with an option to extend; export formats can be JSON/NDJSON or S3 dump. We'll add explicit retention windows to the DPA redline.

[00:35:00] Aisha Khan: On IP ownership - we want the MSA to confirm outputs are the customer's IP.
[00:35:10] Priya Patel: Our standard is that customer-provided data and generated outputs are customer data; we'll ensure language is clear in the MSA.

[00:36:40] James Holloway: Any blockers you foresee on Redwood side to meeting our 11/24 timeline?
[00:36:50] Maya Chen: Internally none; legal will need the 48-hour breach notification ask to evaluate, but we aim to get a proposed redline by 11/17. Pricing and security artifacts are straightforward.

[00:38:12] Ravi Patel: A small tech question: can we get a separate test tenancy for the pilot that routes through our VPC?
[00:38:25] Diego Ramos: For Dedicated/Private we can set up a test cluster in your region and connect via VPC peering. For hosted pilot, we can give a pinned region and temporary token but not VPC peering. We'll propose the dedicated test cluster for your latency needs.

[00:40:00] Sophie Liu: About pen tests - do you share the full report or only executive summary? We typically require the full pen test under NDA.
[00:40:12] Priya Patel: We can share full reports under NDA; we'll add that to the security packet and provide redacted public summaries otherwise.

[00:42:00] Maya Chen: Ok recap: Maya to send redlined MSA + consolidated DPA by 2026-11-17; Diego to send security packet (SOC2, pen test, KMS, network diagrams) by 2026-11-18; Pricing sheet with Dedicated vs hosted numbers and add-ons by 2026-11-17; pilot kickoff scheduling for week of 11/30.

[00:43:25] James Holloway: Sounds good. On procurement approvals, if legal signs off by 11/24 we will route the PO and expect onboarding in early Dec.

[00:44:55] Aisha Khan: One clarification: can you confirm the DPA data deletion semantics (complete purge vs retention for logs)? We'll need explicit wording.
[00:45:07] Diego Ramos: We'll provide a data lifecycle table in the DPA: retention for audit logs, purge steps for customer data, and guarantees for backups. We'll specify the timeframe and certs.

[00:47:30] Maya Chen: I'll include clauses for log redaction and the option to opt-out of storing generated outputs in logs.

[00:48:50] Ravi Patel: For the pilot success criteria, we'll ensure we provide a set of technical KPIs: p95 latency < 200ms, throughput X rps, and less than Y% error rate. Diego, can you confirm if those are achievable on Dedicated?
[00:49:05] Diego Ramos: Yes p95 sub-200ms is achievable on Dedicated with optimized kernel selection and KV cache warmup. We'll lay out the recommended instance types and batching.

[00:50:40] Sophie Liu: Any last questions from Redwood?
[00:50:45] Priya Patel: No, just want to align on the legal redlines afterwards.
[00:50:52] Aisha Khan: We'll review the redline and come back with any final asks by 11/21.

[00:52:00] James Holloway: Thanks everyone, appreciate the clear next steps.
[00:52:08] Maya Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up via email with attachments and set up the pilot slot.
[00:52:15] Meeting ended.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional speaker mis-attributes and auto-transcription noise; we retained timestamps but some words reflect casual speech.
